params.body:
## Why

When Home opened, the hero showed the *last* still in the Studio order first. Moving a still to the top of the order made it appear second, right after the bottom one. Giving still 1 the number 9 (a tie with still 9) left the opening image unchanged, so a reorder in the Studio looked like it did nothing. The crossfade speed was fixed in CSS, so editors could not change it.

## What changes

- **Order:** position 1 in the Studio is on screen at load and preloaded; the rest follow in order (`slot()` in `web/src/lib/crossfade.ts`).
- **Studio, order:** the Home hero stills list sorts by `order`. The field has a Dutch title and description, and a warning flags a number used twice. Ties sort by `_id` in GROQ, so they no longer shuffle between builds.
- **Studio, speed:** Site settings > Home hero > "Seconden per beeld" (`heroSecondsPerImage`, 1.5 to 8, empty = 3). The site clamps it to the same bounds.
- **Keyframes:** generated from the count and the seconds, as proportions of one slot. Nine stills at 3 s give the handoff CSS character for character (`web/test/crossfade.test.ts`); the tests fail when the generator is mutated.
- **CSP:** the generated style block is hashed into the page policy from `HomePage.astro`. A component renders too late for that, because the head is already written. No `'unsafe-inline'`. With `prefers-reduced-motion`, one still is shown, now the first.
- **Fresh data:** the build and `gen-redirects.mjs` read the live API instead of the API CDN, so a build started by a publish cannot read content from before that publish.

An orderable-list plugin (drag and drop) was considered and left out: adding it re-resolved the whole lockfile (newer `@sanity/ui` and client), and existing stills would have needed a data migration.

## Verified locally

- `npm test` (39), `astro check` (0 errors), `sanity schema validate` (0/0), `sanity build`.
- I built from a local copy of the production dataset (GROQ evaluated with groq-js). The output is identical to a build from production.
- In a browser, I tracked the visible still over a full cycle for these datasets:
  - today's data: 1 opens, then 2 to 9
  - 1 and 9 swapped: 9 opens, 1 comes last
  - still 1 set to 9 (a tie): 2 opens; 1 and 9 come last, in a fixed order
  - speed 2: about 2 s per still
  - 5 stills at 5 s
  - a single still

  In every case a still was fully opaque at all times, with no console or CSP errors. CSP hash present in the meta tag and in `_headers` for `/` and `/en/`.

## After merge

- The live Home hero opens on still 1 instead of still 9.
- The Studio needs a deploy for the new field, list order and warning: `cd studio && SANITY_STUDIO_PROJECT_ID=wx6h4iqc npx sanity deploy`.
params.title: Hero stills follow their Studio order; seconds per still editable
